# Yoobi School Supplies

## Colorful recycled school and office supplies that donate a matching item to a US classroom with every purchase

Yoobi makes colorful school and office supplies that donate an identical item to a US classroom with every purchase, working through the Kids In Need Foundation. The lineup runs across writing supplies, binders and notebooks, desk tools, and backpacks, built in bright kid-friendly colors and FSC-certified, PVC-free packaging. Each qualifying purchase adds one supply toward a 900-item classroom kit, enough to outfit up to 30 students for a full school year, which then reaches a school where most kids qualify for free or reduced-price meals. Buying Yoobi through Melioryzm gets you bright, classroom-ready supplies and sends matching supplies to a child who would otherwise go without.

## What Does Yoobi Sell?

Yoobi stocks writing supplies, organization and binders, desk tools, and bags, all built in bright colors for the classroom and made with recycled paper, RPET, and recycled PP plastic. A single playful design language and the same one-for-one giving carry across every line, so the choice is mostly about which supplies a student or office needs.

The table below maps Yoobi's four product categories to what each includes and the student or buyer it fits.

| Category | What it includes | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Writing supplies | Pencils, ballpoint and gel pens, highlighters, markers | Daily classwork and the first-day pouch |
| Organization and binders | One-inch binders, spiral and composition notebooks, journals | Keeping a full school year sorted |
| Desk supplies | Scissors, tape and dispensers, pencil sharpeners, erasers | The home desk or classroom supply caddy |
| Bags | Backpacks, lunch bags, pencil cases, matched sets | The daily carry to and from school |

For most students the writing and organization rows are the year-one default, while the bags row is the bigger-ticket buy that drives the largest single Classroom Pack donation per order.

### Yoobi Writing Supplies

Yoobi writing supplies cover pencils, ballpoint and retractable pens, gel pens, highlighters, and markers, sized and colored for younger hands. Triangle No. 2 pencils ship pre-sharpened in a 24-pack so a kid can write the first day, and the mini highlighters run about two inches long to fit a pencil pouch instead of rolling loose in a bag. The gel pens come in glitter, metallic, and standard color sets, and reviewers single them out for smooth, consistent ink flow. These bright, low-cost basics make up the core of what the brand sells to kids and students, and the colors are the point rather than an afterthought.

### Yoobi Organization and Notebooks

Yoobi organization gear spans one-inch binders, spiral notebooks, composition books, and journals, the paper goods that keep a school year sorted. Each one-inch binder holds up to 275 sheets and uses easy-open D-rings so pages lie flat instead of bowing at the spine, and the composition and spiral notebooks ship in pastel and celestial multipacks. The hardcover journals run 8.5 by 5.25 inches with 80 college-ruled pages and a ribbon bookmark, sized for a backpack rather than a desk drawer. Every binder, notebook, and journal ships in FSC-certified, PVC-free packaging the brand switched to in 2021.

### Yoobi Backpacks and Bags

Yoobi bags include backpacks, lunch bags, and matched backpack-and-lunch-bag sets built for the daily haul to school. The backpacks add side pockets for a water bottle, a mesh back panel for airflow against a kid's back, and padded arm straps, and the Sweet Dreams backpack-and-lunch-bag set bundles both pieces together. Yoobi pairs them with its pencil cases, including a mini-backpack style and a two-zipper organizer sized to hold standard supplies, so the whole carry system matches. That same RPET and recycled-plastic construction used across the backpacks keeps the bags lighter on landfill than virgin-plastic gear.

## What Makes Yoobi Worth Buying?

What sets Yoobi apart is bright, kid-tested design paired with recycled, responsibly packaged materials, not just a low shelf price. The color-forward look is functional: a two-inch highlighter and a triangular pencil are shaped and sized for small hands and crowded pencil pouches, which is why young students reach for them and reviewers report the pencil cases and pouches holding up across a school year. On the materials side, Yoobi builds products from recycled paper, recycled PET, and recycled PP plastic, prints with soy-based ink, and uses vegan leather and bamboo paper in select items, while its paper and plastic packaging has been Forest Stewardship Council certified and PVC-free since 2021. FSC certification means the paper traces back to responsibly managed forests under an independent chain-of-custody audit, not a self-declared claim. Across retailers the supplies carry a 4.7-out-of-5 average from more than 8,500 Walmart reviews, the kind of broad, real-world sample that thin marketing copy cannot fake.

## How Yoobi's One-for-One Giving Works

Every qualifying item triggers a matching supply donated into a 30-student classroom kit, assembled with the brand's charity partner, the Kids In Need Foundation. That model is what Yoobi was built on, and it runs in three named parts.

- One-for-one donation: every qualifying purchase puts one Yoobi supply into a shared classroom kit, and once a kit holds enough for 30 students it ships, carrying 900 items in all, among them pens, pencils, glue sticks, rulers, folders, scissors, crayons, colored pencils, and markers, enough to stock a class for the year.
- The charity partner: a national 501(c)(3) headquartered in Dayton, Ohio and Minneapolis, Minnesota, the Foundation runs more than 40 regional resource centers and steers each kit toward schools whose enrollment is 70 percent or more free-and-reduced-meal eligible.
- Tracked impact: Yoobi reports more than 96 million supplies given to over 7 million students to date, and in its FY23 figures alone it sent out 11,559 of these kits and over 5 million supplies, reaching 346,757 students.

The Foundation tie-up and its 501(c)(3) registration are the independently checkable parts, while the cumulative 96 million figure is Yoobi's own running tally, so weight them accordingly when you compare give-back claims.

## Who Yoobi's Giving Reaches

Yoobi's kits land in under-resourced US public-school classrooms where teachers would otherwise pay for the basics themselves, the gap the brand was founded in 2014 to close. The need is concrete: by Yoobi's account more than 99 percent of teachers spend personal money on supplies, and the Foundation steers kits to schools where most pupils qualify for federally subsidized meals, a standard proxy for low household income. Teachers and principals apply for a kit through their nearest regional resource center rather than receiving one at random, so each delivery reaches a verified, requesting classroom. One donation of pencils, glue, and a personalized pencil pouch is a small per-unit thing, yet at the FY23 rate it reached roughly 950 children every school day, which is what a per-purchase model compounds into at scale. If you want supplies whose purchase puts identical supplies in the hands of a child who needs them, that is the case for buying Yoobi here.
